ent_paper_meng_expert_insight_based_mode.summary: Wei Meng's 2025 arXiv paper proposes a simulation-driven REG-CAP framework that maps rare-earth resource dependencies to military equipment, technology generations, and combat capabilities, using HGNN, LSTM, ODEs, and strategic signal functions to model non-kinetic deterrence trajectories under supply disruption.
ent_paper_meng_expert_insight_based_mode.body:
## Overview

This paper proposes a simulation framework based on expert interviews, integrating graph neural networks and dynamic system modeling, to quantify the non-kinetic strategic deterrence pathways of rare earth supply disruptions on U.S. military capabilities. The authors construct a REG-CAP four-layer coupled model and a Security Critical Zone (SCZ) identification mechanism, characterizing a "lag window—fracture intensity" dual-layer mechanism through piecewise functions and ODEs, thereby converting qualitative strategic experience into computable institutional deterrence weights. ent_paper_ullah_three_dimensional_nonlin.name_en: Three-dimensional nonlinear micro/meso-mechanical response of the fibre-reinforced polymer composites
ent_paper_ullah_three_dimensional_nonlin.summary: Presents a 3D multi-scale computational homogenisation framework for predicting the nonlinear micro/meso-mechanical response of fibre-reinforced polymer composites, incorporating matrix plasticity and fibre-matrix decohesion.
ent_paper_ullah_three_dimensional_nonlin.body:
## Overview
A three-dimensional multi-scale computational homogenisation framework is developed for the prediction of nonlinear micro/meso-mechanical response of the fibre-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites. Two dominant damage mechanisms, i.e. matrix elasto-plastic response and fibre-matrix decohesion are considered and modelled using a non-associative pressure dependent paraboloidal yield criterion and cohesive interface elements respectively. A linear-elastic transversely isotropic material model is used to model yarns/fibres within the representative volume element (RVE). A unified approach is used to impose the RVE boundary conditions, which allows convenient switching between linear displacement, uniform traction and periodic boundary conditions. ent_paper_tomizawa_velocity_jump_in_the_.name: Velocity jump in the crack propagation induced on a semi-crystalline polymer sheet by constant-speed stretching
ent_paper_tomizawa_velocity_jump_in_the_.name_en: Velocity jump in the crack propagation induced on a semi-crystalline polymer sheet by constant-speed stretching
ent_paper_tomizawa_velocity_jump_in_the_.summary: This paper reports the first experimental observation of a crack-propagation velocity jump in a non-elastomer, semi-crystalline polymer sheet under constant-speed stretching, and interprets the jump using glass-transition dynamics near the crack tip.
ent_paper_tomizawa_velocity_jump_in_the_.body:
## Overview
For a long time, the phenomenon of abrupt jumps in crack propagation speed under strain has been well known in elastomers, but such jumps have never been reported in polymers lacking a rubbery plateau (i.e., no rubbery plateau in the storage modulus plot). In this study, by stretching semi-crystalline polymer sheets at a constant rate, crack propagation speed jumps were observed for the first time in such materials without a rubbery plateau. The paper discusses the advantages of constant-rate tensile crack propagation tests and, based on a recently proposed theory of crack speed jumps, provides a physical interpretation for the observed speed jumps in non-elastomeric sheets.

ent_report_oceanwall_rare_earth_bottlene.summary: An Oceanwall research note from July 2025 arguing that advanced robots, particularly humanoids, rely on NdFeB permanent magnets, and that China's dominance in rare earth refining creates a geopolitical supply-chain risk.
ent_report_oceanwall_rare_earth_bottlene.body:
## Overview

This Oceanwall research note (24 July 2025) examines the explosive growth potential of humanoid and industrial robotics alongside a critical upstream bottleneck: rare earth permanent magnets. The note argues that advanced robots, particularly humanoids, depend on neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) magnets to power compact, high-torque electric motors.

## Key Claims

- **Material dependency**: Each humanoid robot may require several kilograms of NdFeB permanent magnets.
- **Supply concentration**: China currently controls approximately 91% of refined rare earth production, creating an acute geopolitical and supply-chain risk.

ent_mat_neodymium_magnet.name: Neodymium-Iron-Boron Magnet
ent_mat_neodymium_magnet.summary: A high-performance rare-earth permanent magnet widely used in servo motors, electric vehicle motors, and high-precision actuators.
ent_mat_neodymium_magnet.body:
## Overview

Neodymium-Iron-Boron Magnet is a rare-earth permanent magnet material primarily composed of neodymium, iron, and boron. It is currently the commercial permanent magnet with the highest magnetic energy product and the strongest overall magnetic performance. In the field of humanoid robots, it serves as the magnetic field source for core actuation components such as Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSM) and frameless torque motors, directly determining the torque density, efficiency, and temperature rise characteristics of joint motors. ent_material_al_mg_alloy_humanoid.summary: A structural lightweighting material system combining high-strength aluminum alloys and magnesium alloys, widely used in humanoid robot frames, joints, and shells to reduce weight while maintaining rigidity.
ent_material_al_mg_alloy_humanoid.body:
## Overview

Aluminum-magnesium alloys are the core material system in the lightweight structures of humanoid robots, using aluminum alloys as the primary skeleton and magnesium alloys as auxiliary weight-reduction measures, significantly reducing overall machine weight while ensuring structural stiffness and strength. What it truly changes is not the replacement of a single material, but the overall paradigm of humanoid robot structural design—a mass allocation logic that shifts from "steel as the bone" to "aluminum-magnesium as the bone, topology optimization as the soul."

ent_material_sic_gan_power_devices.name: SiC/GaN Power Device Materials
ent_material_sic_gan_power_devices.summary: Wide-bandgap semiconductor materials—silicon carbide (SiC) and gallium nitride (GaN)—that enable higher-efficiency, higher-frequency power conversion in motor drives and power electronics.
ent_material_sic_gan_power_devices.body:
## Overview

SiC/GaN power device materials form the core material system of wide-bandgap semiconductors (WBG), where GaN is typically epitaxially grown on heterogeneous substrates (Si, SiC, sapphire) in a wurtzite structure. Due to the lack of inversion symmetry in the wurtzite structure, spontaneous polarization and piezoelectric polarization exist at the GaN/AlGaN heterointerface. The polarization discontinuity induces a high-concentration two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) at the interface, giving GaN HEMTs extremely low on-resistance and ultra-high switching speeds. ent_material_rare_earth_supply.summary: The upstream supply chain of rare-earth elements—especially neodymium, dysprosium, and terbium—used in high-performance permanent magnets for actuators.
ent_material_rare_earth_supply.body:
## Overview

The rare-earth supply chain refers to the entire industrial chain from rare-earth ore mining, smelting and separation, and metal preparation to the processing of high-performance permanent magnet materials (such as NdFeB). It serves as the upstream material foundation for servo motors and frameless torque motors in humanoid robots. What it truly changes is not the performance parameters of a single robot component, but rather **the entire design constraint chain of "how small a motor can be and how much torque it can output" is shifted upstream to the geological and smelting stages**—the stability of rare-earth supply directly determines the cost curve and production ramp-up pace of humanoid robot mass production.

## Overview
The humanoid robot lithium-ion battery system is an electrochemical energy storage solution that provides mobile power for bipedal or wheeled humanoid robots, covering cell chemistry selection, battery pack topology design, thermal management, and safety protection. What it truly changes is not the robot's "range number," but rather **turning the triangular trade-off between energy density, power density, and safety into a hard constraint on the robot's structural design**—the size and weight of the battery pack directly determine torso space allocation and center of mass position.
